proposals.before: Ministers argued that the boy emperor required a regent and urged her to follow the precedent of Han Empress Dowager He.
proposals.after: Ministers argued that the boy emperor required a regent and urged her to follow the precedent of Han Empress Hexi.
proposals.reason: 和熹 is the posthumous title Hexi, not the surname He.

proposals.before: The assembled ministers memorialized: the Son of Heaven is young and tender; it is fitting to follow the precedent of Empress Dowager He of Han.
proposals.after: The assembled ministers memorialized: the Son of Heaven is young and tender; it is fitting to follow the precedent of Empress Hexi of Han.
proposals.reason: Chinese 漢和熹皇后 is Empress Hexi of Han, not Empress He.

proposals.before: Empress Du the Chenggong had the taboo personal name Lingyang; she was a person of Jingzhao and was the great-granddaughter of the General Who Guards the South, Yu.
proposals.after: Empress Du the Chenggong had the taboo personal name Lingyang; she was a person of Jingzhao and was the great-granddaughter of the General Who Guards the South, Du Yu.
proposals.reason: 預 here is Du Yu; the given name alone conceals the identity.

proposals.before: Xuan district's Lingyang county was changed to Guangyang county.
proposals.after: Lingyang county in Xuancheng commandery was changed to Guangyang county.
proposals.reason: 宣城 is Xuancheng commandery, not Xuan district.

proposals.before: Empress Chu the Kangxian (Healthy and Presented).
proposals.after: Empress Chu the Kangxian.
proposals.reason: 康獻 is the compound posthumous title Kangxian; splitting it into Healthy and Presented is a false etymological gloss.

proposals.before: My late sister-consort was yielding and gentle, ever seeking to follow Earth's way; she deferred to the court's wishes because she put the state first.
proposals.after: The late empress was yielding and gentle, ever seeking to follow Earth's way; she deferred to the court's wishes because she put the state first.
proposals.reason: 先后 means the previous empress, not a sister-consort.

proposals.before: Minister Yin Rong, citing Zheng Xuan, ruled that General Who Guards the Wei Chu Pou should observe full court etiquette inside the palace, but on days when the dowager visited her natal home they might behave as father and daughter.
proposals.after: Minister Yin Rong, citing Zheng Xuan, ruled that General of the Guards Chu Pou should observe full court etiquette inside the palace, but on days when the dowager visited her natal home they might behave as father and daughter.
proposals.reason: 衛將軍 is the Jin office General of the Guards, not a general who guards Wei.

proposals.before: Minister of Ceremonies Yin Rong argued according to Zheng Xuan's meaning: when General Who Guards the Wei Pou was within the palace precincts then full ministerial respect; on days when the Empress Dowager returned to comfort her parents, naturally like family-person rites.
proposals.after: Minister of Ceremonies Yin Rong argued according to Zheng Xuan's meaning: when General of the Guards Pou was within the palace precincts then full ministerial respect; on days when the Empress Dowager returned to comfort her parents, naturally like family-person rites.
proposals.reason: 衛將軍 is General of the Guards; Wei is not a toponym here.

proposals.before: Shang leaned by the door before viewing several lines of the memorial, then said, 'I myself originally suspected this'; reaching halfway then stopped, demanded brush and replied to the memorial saying: 'The not-yet-dead person encounters these hundred griefs; moved in thought for the living and dead, the heart therein is as if cut.'
proposals.after: Still leaning by the door she viewed several lines of the memorial, then said, 'I myself originally suspected this'; reaching halfway then stopped, demanded a brush and replied to the memorial saying: 'The not-yet-dead person encounters these hundred griefs; moved in thought for the living and dead, the heart therein is as if cut.'
proposals.reason: 尚 here is the adverb still, not the personal name Shang; the subject remains the Empress Dowager.

proposals.before: To the emperor she was a cousin's widow, so the court debated what mourning he should wear for her.
proposals.after: To the emperor she was a cousin's wife, so the court debated what mourning he should wear for her.
proposals.reason: 從嫂 names the living kinship (wife of a male cousin), not widowhood; widowhood is only the occasion of the mourning debate.

proposals.before: Her father was Bing; she herself has a biography.
proposals.after: Her father was Bing; he has his own biography.
proposals.reason: 自有傳 refers to the father's separate biography, not to the empress.

proposals.before: The Emperor summoned Wang Bao as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, thereby to please the empress's intent.
proposals.after: The Emperor summoned Prince Bao as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, thereby to please the empress's intent.
proposals.reason: 王褒 is Prince Bao (長沙王褒), not a man surnamed Wang; the idiomatic rendering already has Sima Bao.

proposals.before: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict saying: 'The Grand Consort of Kuaiji had the virtue of the civil mother; her fine reputation had fusion; she bore and carried sagely brightness; glory extended to Jin.
proposals.after: In the nineteenth year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict saying: 'The Grand Consort of Kuaiji had the virtue of Wenmu; her fair fame endures; she bore sagely brightness; glory extended to Jin.
proposals.reason: 文母 is the Zhou exemplar Wenmu, not a generic civil mother; 徽音有融 is the Shijing idiom that fair fame endures.

proposals.before: She dreamed repeatedly of twin dragons cradled in her lap and of sun and moon sliding into her bosom; she told her companions she took this for a blessing. When the prince heard, he was intrigued—soon she gave birth to the future Emperor Xiaowu, Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, and the elder princess of Poyang.
proposals.after: She dreamed repeatedly of twin dragons cradled in her lap and of sun and moon sliding into her bosom; she told her companions she took this for a blessing. When the prince heard, he was intrigued—soon she gave birth to the future Emperor Xiaowu, Prince Wenxiao of Kuaiji, and the elder princess of Poyang.
proposals.reason: This unit names 会稽文孝王, not 道子; inserting Daozi invents a personal name the sentence does not use.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Yonghe, mother and son together lost the Emperor's favor; both were secretly deposed; the empress thereupon from grief died.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Yonghe, mother and son together lost the prince's favor; both were confined and deposed; the empress thereupon died of grief.
proposals.reason: In Yonghe 4 Jianwen was still Prince of Kuaiji, so 帝意 is the prince favor; 幽废 is confinement and deposition.

proposals.before: Empress Wang's personal name was Shen'ai; she came from Linyi in Langya commandery.
proposals.after: Empress Wang the Anxi's personal name was Shen'ai; she came from Linyi in Langya commandery.
proposals.reason: The Chinese title 安僖王皇后 includes the posthumous name Anxi, which the idiomatic English drops.

proposals.before: Renowned for beauty and skill at song and lute, she entered the palace as a Shuyuan lady and bore Emperors An and Gong.
proposals.after: Renowned for beauty and skill at song and lute, she entered the palace as a Shuyuan lady and bore Emperor An and Emperor Gong.
proposals.reason: Emperors An fuses the title and first designation ungrammatically; the Chinese names two emperors, An and Gong.

proposals.before: Lady Feng was slender grace; beauty lush and softly yielding.
proposals.after: Lady Fen was slender grace; beauty lush and softly yielding.
proposals.reason: 芬 is Fen, not Feng; the idiomatic rendering invents a different reading.

proposals.before: Each avoided Huayang's blame; ultimately trod Harmonious and Bright's tracks; preserved decline to achieve end—what was fortunately attained was indeed much.
proposals.after: Each avoided Huayang's blame; ultimately trod Hexi's tracks; preserved decline to achieve end—what was fortunately attained was indeed much.
proposals.reason: 和熹 is the posthumous name Hexi of Deng Sui, not the adjectives Harmonious and Bright.

proposals.before: At first she had favor and bore Emperor Ming and Prince Ai of Langya; on this account she was envied by Empress Yu.
proposals.after: At first she had favor and bore Emperor Ming and Pou, Prince of Langya; on this account she was envied by Empress Yu.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王裒 is the Prince of Langya whose personal name is 裒 (Pou, i.e. Sima Pou); the character 裒 is not a posthumous title and is not read Ai. The same prince is called 孝王 (Prince Xiao) in s0206, so Ai is also not his posthumous title.

proposals.before: She once enjoyed the emperor's favor and gave birth to Emperor Ming and Prince Ai of Langya, which drew Empress Yu's jealousy.
proposals.after: She once enjoyed the emperor's favor and gave birth to Emperor Ming and Sima Pou, Prince of Langya, which drew Empress Yu's jealousy.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王裒 names the Prince of Langya by his personal name 裒 (Pou); 裒 is not read Ai and is not a posthumous title. The same prince appears as 孝王 (Prince Xiao) in s0206. Paired with the literal-field repair.

proposals.before: In the midst of the Taining era, Emperor Ming recalled with gratitude the kindness of his foster mother and gifted Yu's wife the Lady Wang as Mistress of Yiyang district, and his mother's younger sister, the wife of the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Xinye Wang Han, as Mistress of Pingyang township.
proposals.after: In the midst of the Taining era, Emperor Ming recalled with gratitude the kindness of his foster mother and gifted Yu's wife the Lady Wang as Mistress of Yiyang district, and his maternal aunt, the wife of the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Han of Xinye, as Mistress of Pingyang township.
proposals.reason: 散騎常侍新野王罕 is the Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Han of Xinye: 新野 is his place of origin and 王 his surname, not the title Prince of Xinye (a prince would not be styled with a surname and given name in this way). 從母 is a maternal aunt and does not specify younger.

proposals.before: During the Taining years, Emperor Ming remembered how Yu's wife had raised him and ennobled her as Mistress of Yiyang county; his aunt, wife of Wang Han, Prince of Xinye and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, received the title Mistress of Pingyang township.
proposals.after: During the Taining years, Emperor Ming remembered how Yu's wife had raised him and ennobled her as Mistress of Yiyang county; his aunt, wife of Wang Han of Xinye, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, received the title Mistress of Pingyang township.
proposals.reason: 新野王罕 is Wang Han of Xinye (surname 王, native place 新野), not a Prince of Xinye. Paired with the literal repair.

proposals.before: She died in the third month of the seventh year of her reign, aged twenty-one.
proposals.after: She died in the third month of the seventh year of Xiankang, aged twenty-one.
proposals.reason: 七年 continues the Xiankang era dated in s0046 (咸康二年); it is not the seventh year of her reign (she had been empress since Xiankang 2, cf. 在位六年 in s0053).

proposals.before: Lingyang county in Xuancheng commandery was renamed Guangyang to avoid the imperial personal name.
proposals.after: Lingyang county in Xuancheng commandery was renamed Guangyang to avoid the empress's personal name.
proposals.reason: The renaming of 陵陽縣 follows from the empress personal name 陵陽 (s0044), not from the emperor's name.

proposals.before: The Han Harmonious and Bright and Shunlie, both also attended court; the recent Mingmu precedent—take them as former models.
proposals.after: Hexi and Shunlie of Han both also attended court; the recent Mingmu precedent—take them as former models.
proposals.reason: 和熹 and 順烈 are both posthumous titles of Han empresses dowager; rendering 和熹 as the gloss Harmonious and Bright while leaving Shunlie romanized is inconsistent and obscures the title, and conflicts with the accepted s0330 repair (Empress Hexi of Han).

proposals.before: The orphan daughter of my late cousin He Zhun, once a supernumerary gentleman-in-attendance, has not yet mastered domestic training and barely knows how to dress presentably.
proposals.after: The orphan daughter of my late cousin He Zhun, once a Cavalier Gentleman-in-Attendance, has not yet mastered domestic training and barely knows how to dress presentably.
proposals.reason: 散騎侍郎 is Cavalier Gentleman-in-Attendance (as in the literal field); nothing in the source says supernumerary (員外).

proposals.before: Again We caused concurrent Grand Guardian, Prince of Wuling Xi, concurrent Grand Commandant, Central Commander Xia, bearing credentials to present the patent and establish as empress.
proposals.after: Again We caused concurrent Grand Guardian, Prince of Wuling Xi, concurrent Grand Commandant, Central Commander Qia, bearing credentials to present the patent and establish as empress.
proposals.reason: 洽 is read Qià; Xia is a misreading.

proposals.before: They next dispatched Grand Guardian Sima Xi, Prince of Wuling, and concurrent Grand Commandant Xie Xia, Central Commander, bearing credentials to invest her as empress.
proposals.after: They next dispatched Grand Guardian Sima Xi, Prince of Wuling, and concurrent Grand Commandant Qia, Central Commander, bearing credentials to invest her as empress.
proposals.reason: The source gives only the given name 洽 (Qià) with the office 中領軍; Xia misreads 洽 and the surname Xie is unsupported by the chapter.

proposals.before: Empress Yu the Xiaoxiao of the Deposed Emperor had the taboo personal name Daolian and was a person from Yanling in Yingchuan.
proposals.after: Empress Yu the Xiao of the Deposed Emperor had the taboo personal name Daolian and was a person from Yanling in Yingchuan.
proposals.reason: 廢帝孝庾皇后 carries the single-character posthumous title 孝 (Xiao); Xiaoxiao duplicates it.

proposals.before: In the first year of Jianwu, she was taken as Princess Consort of Langya and had great favor.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jianwu, she was taken as a Lady (furen) of the Prince of Langya and had great favor.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王夫人 is a furen (Lady) of the Prince of Langya, a rank below the princess consort (妃); s0201 confirms she remained only a 夫人 after his accession.

proposals.before: In the first year of Jianwu he took her as Princess Consort of Langya and favored her deeply.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jianwu he took her as a Lady (furen) of the Prince of Langya and favored her deeply.
proposals.reason: 琅邪王夫人 is a furen of the Prince of Langya, not his princess consort (妃); s0201 says she was still only a 夫人.

proposals.before: The Emperor asked the reason; she replied saying: 'Your concubine has younger sisters; the middle one has already married Prince of Changsha Bao; the remaining two younger sisters have not yet been matched; I fear elder sister having become someone's concubine, there will again be none who seek them.'
proposals.after: The Emperor asked the reason; she replied saying: 'Your concubine has younger sisters; the middle one has already married Wang Bao of Changsha; the remaining two younger sisters have not yet been matched; I fear elder sister having become someone's concubine, there will again be none who seek them.'
proposals.reason: 長沙王褒 is Wang Bao of Changsha (native place 長沙, surname 王); s0199 calls him 王褒 and has him appointed a mere Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, impossible for an imperial prince.

proposals.before: When he asked why, she said: "I have sisters—the middle one has married Prince Sima Bao of Changsha, but the two youngest are still unwed. Men may think that because I am only a concubine, they need not court my sisters."
proposals.after: When he asked why, she said: "I have sisters—the middle one has married Wang Bao of Changsha, but the two youngest are still unwed. Men may think that because I am only a concubine, they need not court my sisters."
proposals.reason: 長沙王褒 is Wang Bao of Changsha, not a Sima prince; s0199 names him 王褒 and appoints him Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

proposals.before: The Emperor summoned Prince Bao as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, thereby to please the empress's intent.
proposals.after: The Emperor summoned Wang Bao as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, thereby to please the empress's intent.
proposals.reason: 王褒 is the personal name Wang Bao (surname 王), not Prince Bao.

proposals.before: He summoned Sima Bao, Prince of Changsha, to serve as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and put her mind at ease.
proposals.after: He summoned Wang Bao to serve as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and put her mind at ease.
proposals.reason: 王褒 is Wang Bao; he was not a Sima prince of Changsha (see s0196).

proposals.before: On xinsi day of the eighth month, the Emperor faced the gallery and dispatched concurrent Grand Guardian Liu Dan to honor her as Empress Dowager; styled Chongxun Palace.'
proposals.after: On xinsi day of the eighth month, the Emperor faced the gallery and dispatched concurrent Grand Guardian Liu Dan to honor her as Empress Dowager; styled Chongxun Palace.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark; this sentence is narrative, not quoted speech.

proposals.before: just viewing the catalpa tree; issuing owl-feathers at Li brightness.
proposals.after: just viewing the catalpa tree; issuing zhen-poison feathers at Li brightness.
proposals.reason: 鴆羽 are feathers of the poisonous zhen bird (i.e. poison), not owl feathers.

proposals.before: Each escaped the stain that befell Yang Zhi of Huayang, trod instead in Deng Sui's footsteps, and steered a fading court to a peaceful close—more good fortune than anyone might expect.
proposals.after: Each escaped the reproach of Huayang, trod instead in Deng Sui's footsteps, and steered a fading court to a peaceful close—more good fortune than anyone might expect.
proposals.reason: The source says only 華陽之釁; it does not name Yang Zhi, and Huayang is not a known designation of Empress Yang Zhi. The idiomatic identification is unsupported; keep the source designation Huayang.

proposals.before: Last promoted Yi and Gui; Bao advanced perishing You.
proposals.after: Mo rose and Gui was laid low; Bao advanced and You perished.
proposals.reason: The line is parallel: 末升夷癸 / 褒進亡幽. 末 (Mo[xi]) rose and 夷 (laid low) 癸 (Gui, i.e. Jie Lügui of Xia), just as 褒 (Bao[si]) advanced and 亡 (destroyed) 幽 (King You). 夷 is a verb, not a person Yi.

proposals.before: Late ages raised Yi and Gui to honor; Bao advanced until You perished.
proposals.after: Mo Xi rose and Gui was laid low; Baosi advanced and King You perished.
proposals.reason: Continue the s0315 idiomatic chain: spell 末(喜)/妹妃 as Mo Xi, the form already used for the same Xia consort in s0307.

proposals.before: Lü's concubine turned the house of Ying; Lady Huang shifted the Mi clan's fate.
proposals.after: Lü's concubine turned the house of Ying; Huang's concubine shifted the Mi clan's fate.
proposals.reason: 黃姬 parallels 呂妾 (Lü's concubine): it is the concubine of a man surnamed Huang, not a lady surnamed Huang.

proposals.before: Emperor Hui received substance; consorts of Wang indulged their viciousness; insight dark as croaking frogs; wisdom dim as patterned clams.
proposals.after: Emperor Hui received substance; as sovereign he indulged his obstinacy; insight dark as croaking frogs; wisdom dim as patterned clams.
proposals.reason: 王縱其嚚 has no reference to consorts or women of a Wang clan; 嚚 is obstinate stupidity, attributed to Emperor Hui, whose dull endowment the clause describes. 王 is read as the sovereign; the Chinese is left unaltered.

proposals.before: Emperor Hui was dull by nature while the Wang women unleashed their malice—his wit was no brighter than a frog's croak, his judgment no sharper than a clam in mud.
proposals.after: Emperor Hui was dull by nature, and as sovereign he gave free rein to his obstinacy—his wit was no brighter than a frog's croak, his judgment no sharper than a clam in mud.
proposals.reason: The source names no Wang women; 王縱其嚚 describes Emperor Hui's obstinate stupidity being given free rein.

proposals.before: Empress Yu, posthumously titled Respectful and Reverent.
proposals.after: Empress Yu, posthumously titled Yuanjing.
proposals.reason: 元敬 is the posthumous title Yuanjing; 元 does not mean Respectful.

proposals.before: Burial beside Yuan Di or shared sacrifice with him would violate ritual propriety."
proposals.after: Burial beside Emperor Yuan or shared sacrifice with him would violate ritual propriety."
proposals.reason: Use the same English title Emperor Yuan used throughout for 元帝.

proposals.before: General Who Conquers the West Yi and Colonel of the Southern Interior Shang argued, saying, 'A father's veneration is exhausted within one family; a ruler's reverence is weighty for all under Heaven; Zheng Xuan's interpretation falls within the mean of feeling and rite.'
proposals.after: General Who Conquers the West Yi and Southern Leader of Court Gentlemen Shang argued, saying, 'A father's veneration is exhausted within one family; a ruler's reverence is weighty for all under Heaven; Zheng Xuan's interpretation falls within the mean of feeling and rite.'
proposals.reason: 南中郎 (南中郎將) is the Southern Leader of Court Gentlemen, a general's post; it is not a colonel and 中郎 is not "Interior".

proposals.before: Yu Yi, General Who Conquers the West, and Xie Shang, Colonel of the Southern Interior, then argued that "a father commands reverence only within the household, whereas the sovereign's dignity weighs on the whole realm—Zheng Xuan's reading strikes the right balance between affection and ritual."
proposals.after: Yu Yi, General Who Conquers the West, and Xie Shang, Southern Leader of Court Gentlemen, then argued that "a father commands reverence only within the household, whereas the sovereign's dignity weighs on the whole realm—Zheng Xuan's reading strikes the right balance between affection and ritual."
proposals.reason: 南中郎 (南中郎將) is the Southern Leader of Court Gentlemen, a general's post; it is not a colonel and 中郎 is not "Interior". Paired with the literal repair.

decisions.reason: s0015 從母散騎常侍新野王罕: the office 散騎常侍 is followed by place + surname + given name, and the s0199 pattern (長沙王褒 = 王褒) confirms the 王 is a surname. "Prince of Xinye" is unsupported, and 從母 does not specify "younger". I accept the repair, though I do not rely on the owner's general claim about princely styling.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太寧中，明帝追懷母養之恩，贈豫妻王氏為䢵陽縣君，從母散騎常侍新野王罕妻為平陽鄉君。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0015: 新野王罕 is Wang Han of Xinye (an official with surname 王), not a prince. It agrees with r0020.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太寧中，明帝追懷母養之恩，贈豫妻王氏為䢵陽縣君，從母散騎常侍新野王罕妻為平陽鄉君。

decisions.reason: s0051 七年三月 continues the era of s0046 (咸康二年), and s0053 后在位六年 fits Xiankang 2–7. "Seventh year of her reign" misreads the date.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 七年三月，后崩，年二十一。

decisions.reason: s0050: the county 陵陽 was renamed because of the empress's personal name 陵陽 (s0044 諱陵陽), not the emperor's.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 改宣城陵陽縣為廣陽縣。

decisions.reason: s0089 漢和熹、順烈 lists two Han posthumous titles in parallel. Glossing only 和熹 is inconsistent, and the accepted s0330 repair uses Hexi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢和熹、順烈，並亦臨朝，近明穆故事，以為先制。

decisions.reason: s0160 故散騎侍郎準: 散騎侍郎 is Cavalier Gentleman-in-Attendance. Nothing says 員外 (supernumerary).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣從祖弟故散騎侍郎準之遺女，未閑教訓，衣履若如人。

decisions.reason: s0162 中領軍洽: the graph 洽 reads Qià; "Xia" is a misreading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又使兼太保、武陵王晞，兼太尉、中領軍洽，持節奉冊立為皇后。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0162: only the given name 洽 appears with his offices. The surname Xie and the reading Xia are both unsupported.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又使兼太保、武陵王晞，兼太尉、中領軍洽，持節奉冊立為皇后。

decisions.reason: s0178 廢帝孝庾皇后: the posthumous title is the single graph 孝. "Xiaoxiao" duplicates it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 廢帝孝庾皇后諱道憐，潁川鄢陵人也。

decisions.reason: s0194 納為琅邪王夫人 makes her a 夫人 (Lady) of the Prince of Langya, not his 妃, and s0201 后雖為夫人 confirms she stayed at that rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建武元年，納為琅邪王夫人，甚有寵。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0194: 琅邪王夫人 is a furen, not the princess consort, per s0201 后雖為夫人.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建武元年，納為琅邪王夫人，甚有寵。

decisions.reason: s0196 長沙王褒 is Wang Bao of Changsha. s0199 帝召王褒為尚書郎 names him 王褒 and gives him a junior Secretariat post, which rules out an imperial prince.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝問其故，對曰：「妾有妹，中者已適長沙王褒，餘二妹未有所適，恐姊為人妾，無復求者。」

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0196: Wang Bao of Changsha, not a Sima prince (s0199 王褒…尚書郎).

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝問其故，對曰：「妾有妹，中者已適長沙王褒，餘二妹未有所適，恐姊為人妾，無復求者。」

decisions.reason: s0199 帝召王褒為尚書郎: 王褒 is the personal name Wang Bao, not "Prince Bao".

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝召王褒為尚書郎，以悅后意。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0199: Wang Bao, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; no Sima prince of Changsha is involved.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝召王褒為尚書郎，以悅后意。

decisions.reason: s0248 is narrative (八月辛巳，帝臨軒…), so the stray closing quotation mark in the literal is an error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 八月辛巳，帝臨軒，遣兼太保劉耽尊為皇太后，稱崇訓宮。

decisions.reason: s0305 鴆羽 are feathers of the zhen poison bird; "owl feathers" mistranslates 鴆.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 方觀梓樹，頒鴆羽於離明。

decisions.reason: s0313 各免華陽之釁 names only 華陽, and nothing in the chapter equates it with Yang Zhi, so removing that identification is right. Residual, filed separately: the same idiomatic sentence still renders 和熹 as "Deng Sui", a personal name absent from the chapter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 各免華陽之釁，竟躡和熹之蹤，保陵遲以克終，所幸實為多矣。

decisions.reason: s0315 末升夷癸，褒進亡幽 is a parallel couplet: 夷 (laid low) matches 亡 (destroyed), so 夷 is a verb, not a person "Yi". 末 is the Xia consort, as in s0307 妹妃.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 末升夷癸，褒進亡幽。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0315: spelling the Xia consort Mo Xi (末 / 妹妃) matches s0307 and the s0315 literal repair r0038.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 末升夷癸，褒進亡幽。

decisions.reason: s0326 呂妾變嬴，黃姬化羋 is parallel: 黃姬 is the concubine of the Huang man, as 呂妾 is the Lü man's concubine. "Lady Huang" is not supported. Medium confidence, accepted as the better parallel reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 呂妾變嬴，黃姬化羋。

decisions.reason: s0302 王縱其嚚 says nothing about women of a Wang clan. 嚚 (obstinate stupidity) describes the ruler given free rein. The repair removes an invented reference without altering the Chinese; medium confidence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0302: no "Wang women" are in 王縱其嚚. It matches r0041.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。

decisions.reason: s0001 元敬虞皇后: 元敬 is the posthumous title Yuanjing, and 元 does not mean "Respectful".

sourceWitness.excerpt: 元敬虞皇后

decisions.reason: s0221: 元帝 should be rendered Emperor Yuan, as everywhere else in the chapter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若乃祔葬配食，則義所不可。」

decisions.reason: s0102 南中郎尚: 南中郎 (南中郎將) is the Southern Leader of Court Gentlemen, a general's post, not a colonel and not "Interior".

sourceWitness.excerpt: 征西將軍翼、南中郎尚議謂「父尊盡於一家，君敬重於天下，鄭玄義合情禮之中」。

decisions.reason: Idiomatic s0102: the same correction of 南中郎 as r0045. (The idiomatic's supplied surnames Yu and Xie are a separate name-claim finding.)

sourceWitness.excerpt: 征西將軍翼、南中郎尚議謂「父尊盡於一家，君敬重於天下，鄭玄義合情禮之中」。

proposals.before: The Lady Pei had the name Mu; she was granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Chuo, daughter of the Registrar of the Grand Tutor Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.
proposals.after: The Lady Pei had the name Mu; she was granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Chuo, daughter of the Registrar of the Grand Tutor Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yifu.
proposals.reason: 太尉王夷甫 gives only the courtesy name 夷甫 (Yifu). The personal name Yan 衍 appears nowhere in the chapter, so the literal must render the name the source gives. One repetition in this field.

proposals.before: Lady Pei was named Mu—granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Pei Chuo, daughter of the Grand Tutor's registrar Pei Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.
proposals.after: Lady Pei was named Mu—granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Pei Chuo, daughter of the Grand Tutor's registrar Pei Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yifu.
proposals.reason: 太尉王夷甫 gives only the courtesy name 夷甫 (Yifu); 'Wang Yan' supplies an outside personal name. Same correction as the literal field; one repetition.

proposals.before: Han empresses dowager Deng and Liang both held court, as did our own late Empress Mingmu—let their example be your guide.
proposals.after: The Han empresses dowager Hexi and Shunlie both held court, as did our own late Empress Mingmu—let their example be your guide.
proposals.reason: 漢和熹、順烈 names the Han empresses only by their posthumous titles 和熹 and 順烈; the surnames Deng and Liang are outside knowledge. Keeps the English consistent with the literal (Hexi and Shunlie) and with the corrected name claims for p050/p051.

proposals.before: Each escaped the reproach of Huayang, trod instead in Deng Sui's footsteps, and steered a fading court to a peaceful close—more good fortune than anyone might expect.
proposals.after: Each escaped the reproach of Huayang, trod instead in Empress Hexi's footsteps, and steered a fading court to a peaceful close—more good fortune than anyone might expect.
proposals.reason: 竟躡和熹之蹤 gives only the posthumous title 和熹; the personal name Deng Sui 鄧綏 is outside knowledge. Matches the literal (Hexi's tracks) and the corrected name claims for p187.

decisions.reason: Checked s0063 太尉王夷甫外孫: the source gives only the courtesy name 夷甫 (Yifu), and 衍 never appears in the chapter. The literal must render 'Wang Yifu', which resolves my round-1 s0063 finding. There is one repetition in this field, and the after text changes nothing else.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 裴氏名穆，長水校尉綽孫，太傅主簿遐女，太尉王夷甫外孫。

decisions.reason: The same s0063 correction in the idiomatic field: 太尉王夷甫 gives the courtesy name 夷甫, so 'Wang Yan' was an outside personal name. 'Grand Commandant Wang Yifu' matches the literal (r0047) and the p030 label. There is one repetition, and the rest of the sentence is unchanged.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太尉王夷甫外孫

decisions.reason: Checked s0089 漢和熹、順烈: the Han empresses dowager are named only by the posthumous titles 和熹 and 順烈, and the surnames Deng and Liang are outside knowledge. 'Hexi and Shunlie' matches the accepted literal r0024 and the p050/p051 name claims. Adding 'The' at the start is only grammatical.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢和熹、順烈，並亦臨朝

decisions.reason: Checked s0313 竟躡和熹之蹤: 和熹 is only the posthumous title of the Han empress dowager (Hexi); the personal name Deng Sui (鄧綏) is absent from the chapter. 'Empress Hexi's footsteps' matches the literal 'Hexi's tracks', the accepted s0330 repair and the p187 label. Before equals my accepted r0037 after; after equals the current applied text.
